patterns.why_it_works: Side by side, the only differences left are shape, size and color, which is what the buyer is comparing. A tile on another ground reads as another kind of product or as a mistake.
patterns.for_earf: 'The family.' and the color switcher on https://www.earf.world/ show four studio pictures on three grounds: Tropos on warm white, Mantle on spot-lit gray, Hemisphere and Core on near-black, with two light text panels and two dark ones. Put all four on one ground with one shadow and one camera height, Hemisphere hung from the top edge of its tile, the four text panels one color. The stores' ground is always a light neutral; the rule that carries over is 'one', not 'light'. For the lamps the stores show two ways: switched off in the grid, with the lit view second on the product page (DWR, Fritz Hansen, Hem, Muuto); or lit on the light ground (Carl Hansen RF200 picture 1, Hem Coco picture 2). The gallery already holds an unlit Hemisphere and an unlit Core row, but on dark and mid gray, and Mantle on a third gray: those three need new renders on the Tropos ground, in eight tints each. Tropos has its eight.

patterns.why_it_works: Picture 1 answers what it is. The rooms answer how big it is and where it goes. The close-ups answer what it is made of. A visitor who sees only the first picture still knows the object.
patterns.for_earf: Tropos pages open with the place picture; the plain-ground front is second. Order to use: front; a listening room; details (horn from behind, amplifier); the turning horn; the bar; the place. Today the counts are Tropos 5 (6 in Acid), Hemisphere 9, Core 4, Mantle 3, and the only room on the site is the bar at night; no picture shows a product in a home by day. The brand-run stores with full sets show 6 to 32 pictures per product and 2 to 31 different rooms. A set per product that matches the leaner full sets (Hem, Carl Hansen): Tropos 7: front; three-quarter from behind; turning horn; amplifier; a pair in a living room by day with a sofa or chair for size; bar; place. Mantle 6: studio; with cover; from above with a record on; arm and platter close; on a sideboard at home; bar. Hemisphere 8: off; lit, same frame; from below; cap; over a dining table with chairs and plates by day; the same at night; group; all eight. Core 7: off; lit, same frame; beside a glass or a book for size; on a bedside table or shelf by day; the same in the evening; bar; all eight. Real rooms and customers (DWR, Hem, Vitra, USM, Muuto show them) are not possible before something is built; the render notice in the footer stays until then.

patterns.why_it_works: The buyer sees the chosen color clearly once, and sees the object at home in several colors. Nobody has to make every room in every color.
patterns.for_earf: Eight tints do not mean eight of every picture. Today five Tropos views and six Hemisphere views exist once per tint (front, horn, amplifier, place, turn; lit, below, table, off, cap, rim), while 'bar' and 'all eight' are already shared. For the new room pictures do what the stores do: render each room once, each in a different tint (a living room with an Ice pair, a sideboard with an Ember Mantle, a dinner table under Dust pendants), and show the same room set on all eight pages after the tint's own plain-ground pictures. That is about 32 tint pictures on the common ground (64 with the lamps' off and lit pairs) plus roughly 20 shared pictures for the whole site, not 8 times every view.

patterns.for_earf: Hemisphere has 'Lit' first and 'Off' fifth, from different set-ups (near-black against dark gray). Core has no single unlit picture, only the row of eight by day. Make an off and lit pair per lamp from one camera on one ground and place them first and second. Do the same once in a room: Core on a shelf by day and in the evening; Hemisphere over a table by day and at night.

patterns.for_earf: Core (a 160 mm ball) today appears alone on black, on the bar at night, and in rows of eight. Add Core on a bedside table, a bookshelf niche or a dinner table beside a glass and a book. Mantle appears on gray and on the bar; add it on a sideboard with a record sleeve leaning beside it and a record on the platter. Hemisphere over a table appears once, small, in a dark room; the stores hang pendants over set tables with chairs in the frame (9 of DWR's 12 Saucer pictures, 31 of Muuto's 32). Only things that would really stand there, nothing staged to hide a cable or a base.

patterns.why_it_works: Nothing covers the picture. A list works the same with a finger as with a mouse. The count or the names tell at once how many things in the picture can be bought. Every picture is treated the same, so the visitor learns the control once.
patterns.for_earf: The hero on https://www.earf.world/ now carries four white dots, one per product; no store among the ten puts marks on its home page's first picture, and five of the six that link room pictures to products use a corner control or a line of names. Two ways to follow them: one corner control on the hero ('4 pieces') that opens a list of four rows (plain-ground thumb, name, kind, 'See Tropos'); or one line under the hero with the four names as links, as HAY does. If the dots stay, Vitra's rules as seen: on the cabinet body, never on a driver, a lamp's light or the record; a card with cut-out, name and one action; a list button for those who miss the dots; and the same treatment on every room picture on the site (the bar pictures on the product pages and the lighting page), not on the hero alone.

In the place where the stores print the wait, print what is true today: the state of the build and what the reply holds (a quote, a build slot, by when an answer comes). patterns.for_earf: 1. Studio pictures of one family on three grounds side by side in a grid (the only mixed row I saw elsewhere is Fritz Hansen's category row). 2. Lamps shown lit, on black, in grid tiles; the stores' grids show lamps unlit on the common ground. 3. A product gallery that opens with the product in a landscape (Tropos 'Out'); nine of ten open with the product alone on a plain ground and HAY opens with a place of use. 4. Product pictures set where the product cannot be used (lava field, desert, rain); every in-place picture I saw at the stores is a place of use, including outdoors for portable lamps. The way to buy as a small text link that scrolls away (Carl Hansen also uses a text link, but in a column that stays in view). 13. patterns.why_it_works: With one ground, the only things that change from tile to tile are the product and its color, so those are what the buyer compares. A glowing shade reads against taupe, beige and light gray; it does not need black.
patterns.for_earf: Today 'The family.' on https://www.earf.world/ is four tiles in three sizes, four tints and three grounds: Tropos 696 x 1031 on warm white (#e6dfd6), Mantle 696 x 464 on a spotlit gray that runs from #2e2a27 at the corners to #aaa6a3, Hemisphere and Core 340 x 340 on #1b1b1b. Across the four galleries there are five studio grounds (warm white, near-black, dark gray #2e2f30, mid-gray #6c6c6c, spotlit gray). What it means: one studio set for all four products, one camera height, one light, lamps lit in it. 4 products x 8 tints = 32 renders. A mid-tone in the range these stores use (Santa & Cole's taupe, Tala's beige) holds a glow and also shows a clear tint (Fog) and a black one (Smoke). If the owner wants the dark, all four products go on it, as at Roll & Hill. These 32 pictures serve 'The family.', the color switcher and picture 1 of every product page.

patterns.why_it_works: Not applicable. This entry lists differences so that each can be kept on purpose or dropped.
patterns.for_earf: 1 Markers on the products in a picture: four dots on the home hero. The only marker elsewhere is Flos's '+' in the corner of a room picture. 2 Three grounds in one four-tile product grid, and five studio grounds across four products. HAY mixes grounds in a mosaic listing; no store splits one small grid between light and near-black. 3 A product ground as dark as #1b1b1b. The darkest I measured elsewhere were Roll & Hill's #362e2b and Bocci's night tiles at #35322d. 4 Pictures of a product where it cannot be used: eight pictures of a mains loudspeaker in snow, sand, water and fire, one of them the first picture in the Tropos gallery. The nearest is Flos's portable page, cordless outdoor-rated lamps among rocks and trees. 5 A text link as the only action on a product page, with a share link of equal weight beside it, and a mail link that drops the product and tint. 6 The words 'Price on request.' patterns.why_it_works: The buyer compares objects, not pictures. When one tile sits on a different ground it reads as a different kind of thing or as a mistake. In all 13 stores every grid I saw held to one ground; 10 of the 13 use white or pale grey for it.
patterns.for_earf: Live at 08:50 UTC on 20 Nov, 'The family.' and the color switcher still show Tropos on bright warm white, Mantle on spotlit gray, Hemisphere and Core lit on near-black: three grounds in one grid. Put all four on one ground with one light direction and one camera height. EARF's own /tropos page already does it: eight Tropos on one warm white. That means 24 new plain-ground pictures (Mantle, Hemisphere, Core in 8 tints), with the lamps shown as objects on that ground; the lit, dark lamp pictures go in their galleries. No audio store shows a product working in its tile. The owner's taste for deep color has a place the stores also use: a tint-colored ground behind detail crops lower on the page, as B&O does.

patterns.why_it_works: The buyer finds the back, the side and the detail without asking, and nothing looks hidden. For the team it is a checklist: a page either has every picture on the list or it does not.
patterns.for_earf: Today the galleries hold 5 pictures (Tropos; Acid 6), 3 (Mantle), 4 (Core) and 9 (Hemisphere); the stores hold 6 to 15. Write the list and render to it. Tropos: 1 front 3/4 on the common ground, 2 straight front, 3 side, 4 back with the amplifier plate, 5 from above, 6 horn detail, 7 an edge or joint detail of the acrylic, 8 a pair in a listening room, 9 the place picture, 10 the turn. Core: lit, unlit, a detail, in a living room, the row of eight. The same list in all eight tints (today only Acid has the bar picture). Lead with the plain view: 12 of 13 stores open the set with the object alone; EARF's Tropos page opens with the place picture, where the speaker fills about a quarter of the frame. Also the stage: EARF's is 520 px wide in a 1440 window; the six I measured elsewhere are 612 to 803 px.

patterns.pattern: 3. The listening room picture: a pair, set left and right, seen from the seat, with a console, a turntable or a fireplace between them and a sofa or chair in front.
seen_at: Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 and https://www.klipsch.com/products/klipschorn-ak7 (a pair in the two corners, turntable table between, sofa in front)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 and https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/opus-1 (a pair either side of a fireplace, one armchair seen from behind)
KEF: https://us.kef.com/collections/blade-series and https://us.kef.com/
Transparent: https://transpa.rent/us/ (two speakers either side of the turntable rack)
U-Turn Audio: https://uturnaudio.com/ (turntable between two speakers)
Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beolab-28 (a pair in a living room)
patterns.why_it_works: A loudspeaker is bought as a pair for a room. This one picture answers how far apart they stand, how tall they are next to a sofa, and what sits between them. The rooms are lit so the object reads; none is a dark scene.
patterns.for_earf: EARF has no picture of a pair of Tropos in a home listening room; its one room is the dark bar, where each speaker is about 150 px wide. Render one daylight room: two Tropos about 2.5 m apart, a low console between them with the Mantle on it, the back of a chair at the bottom edge. Klipsch shows the same room once per finish; in renders that is a material swap, so all eight tints are within reach. Furniture at true size, so that 1295 mm reads against a 750 mm console. This is the 'listening space image' the owner asked for, in the layout six of these stores share.

patterns.pattern: 4. Markers explain parts on a plain-ground or exploded view. On room pictures they are rare, sit at the object's edge against plain background, and open a card. Nothing is placed on the part the eye goes to.
seen_at: Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (5 numbered rings beside the parts on a white ground; click gives a headline and 1-2 sentences)
Sonos: https://www.sonos.com/en-us/shop/era-300 ('+' on single parts of the exploded view)

KEF: https://us.kef.com/products/ls50-wireless-2 (2 on the exploded driver) and https://us.kef.com/collections/blade-series (room picture: one dot per speaker at the top edge of the cabinet; card with name, availability, colors, arrow)
Transparent: https://transpa.rent/us/transparent-speaker-white ('+' beside each part)
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-reference-10/ (fixed dots on the tonearm with labels beside)
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 (fixed labels beside the parts of the cutaway)
patterns.why_it_works: On a plain ground a marker reads as a control and its label has room. On a dark, busy room picture it competes with the product. A card that opens with a name and an arrow tells the visitor what a click will do before the page changes.
patterns.for_earf: None of the 13 stores puts markers on its home page's first picture; EARF now has 4 white dots on the bar scene. Two courses fit what I saw. (a) Take the dots off the hero; it keeps its two buttons and the four tiles follow directly under it, as at B&O, Transparent, Syng and Avantgarde. (b) Keep them the KEF way: one per product, at the top edge of the object against plain background, each opening a small card with the product's name, one fact and an arrow, and a spoken label ('Show Tropos'). Then apply the same rule to every room picture on the site or to none. Use markers where six stores use them: on one plain-ground view of the Tropos, numbered, set in the ground beside the horn, the compression driver, the woofer, the ports and the amplifier plate.

patterns.pattern: 5. The turning view is one item in the picture set, started by the visitor, at the same size as the stills. The first picture is a still.
seen_at: Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beolab-28 (14 stills stepping around one unit; the composer has a 'Rotation' switch)
KEF: https://us.kef.com/products/ls50-wireless-2 (button '360 View' under the stage loads a model to drag)
OJAS: https://ojas.nyc/products/klipsch-ko-r2 (a turnable 3D model as a gallery item)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 ('Rotate view' swaps front and rear stills)
patterns.why_it_works: The visitor sees the back and the sides without leaving the page and controls the pace. A still loads first, so the page does not wait on a heavy file.
patterns.for_earf: EARF has a turn of the horn only, 640 x 576, as the fifth thumbnail beside stills of 1200 x 1500. Make it the whole speaker, back and amplifier plate included, at stage size, opened by a control with the word or number '360' under the stage, and let the visitor drag or step it. B&O's 14 steps are about one still every 26 degrees, which a render set covers. Do the same for the Mantle.

patterns.pattern: 6. A turntable is shown straight from above, with and without its cover, from the back with its sockets, close on the arm, and on furniture near speakers, usually with a record on.
seen_at: Transparent: https://transpa.rent/us/turntable-black (1 top, 2 cover raised, 3 front, 4 back, 5 side, 6 controls, 7 cartridge, 8 accessories)
U-Turn Audio: https://uturnaudio.com/products/orbit-special-turntable (3/4, cover open, top, 3/4, cover closed)
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3 and https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-10 (top view beside the name; with dust cover; top views in every color; 'Dimensions (lid closed)')
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-evo-2/ (top view, back with sockets, from above in rooms with hands and a sleeve)
Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/turntables/klimax-lp12 and https://www.linn.co.uk/us/turntables (front elevation, arm close-ups, from above, on a console beside a speaker)
patterns.why_it_works: The top is the face of a turntable and the view its owner has every day. The cover changes its look and its height. The sockets and the arm are what the owner handles.
patterns.for_earf: Mantle has 3 pictures: studio 3/4, with its cover, at the bar. Missing against all five stores: the straight top view with a record on; a front elevation; the back with the phono stage's sockets and bypass switch; the arm and cartridge close up (EARF's own table names the arm, a Rega RB330); and a living-room picture on a console between or beside two Tropos. EARF already states the height with the cover on (196 mm), as Rega does.

patterns.pattern: 7. Size is shown in a picture: a view with dimension lines, a ruler, or a body beside the object.
seen_at: Syng: https://syngspace.com/products/cell-alpha-with-floor-stand (a picture in the set with dimension lines and both heights)
OJAS: https://ojas.nyc/products/artbook-shelf-speaker-2 (elevations with ruler scales marked 1 foot) and https://ojas.nyc/products/klipsch-ko-r2 (front and side elevations)
Transparent: https://transpa.rent/us/turntable-black (exploded drawing beside the dimension line)
Teenage Engineering: https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4 (line drawing of the front beside the specs; line drawings of people)
Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9 (a person with a hand on it)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (a man beside it in the film)
patterns.why_it_works: A row that says 1295 mm does not tell most buyers that the speaker reaches chest height. A picture does, and it saves a round of letters.
patterns.for_earf: Tropos is 1295 x 560 x 428 mm and about 73 kg; no picture on the site says so. Add to each gallery one drawn front and side elevation with three dimension lines; for the Mantle a top view with 450 x 360 and the two heights. With renders only, a drawing is the honest form. A rendered person would be the case the owner calls worst; if a body is wanted, a line-drawn figure beside the elevation is what Teenage Engineering uses.

patterns.pattern: 8. The inside, or the object with its cover off, is shown, with the names of the parts set beside them.
seen_at: Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 (grille-off views in the gallery; labeled cutaway)
Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9 (gallery slide with the cover off)
Teenage Engineering: https://teenage.engineering/products/od-11 (grilles off, inside assembly)
Sonos: https://www.sonos.com/en-us/shop/era-300 (exploded view)
KEF: https://us.kef.com/products/ls50-wireless-2 (exploded driver)
Transparent: https://transpa.rent/us/transparent-speaker-white (exploded parts)
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-reference-10/ (labeled tonearm)
patterns.why_it_works: It shows what the money buys and lets named parts stand where adjectives about sound would stand.
patterns.for_earf: Tropos is clear acrylic, so its parts already show, but no picture names them. Use the marker view from pattern 4 and give each label the fact line the site already has (15-inch woofer; 2-inch compression driver on the horn; Hypex FA123; ports; lining). No new words are needed. For the Mantle: plinth, posts, base, belt and motor, arm.

patterns.pattern: 9. The product's name heads the page. The finish is a named choice beside the picture, and choosing one recolors the same view in place.
seen_at: Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9 (all 6 slides swap, scroll position kept, address gets ?variant=)
Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360 (one cutout recolors, caption changes)
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-evo-2/ (one picture, same angle, name line changes)
U-Turn Audio: https://uturnaudio.com/products/orbit-custom
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (recolors inside the same room picture; address gets ?c=)
KEF: https://us.kef.com/products/ls50-wireless-2
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6
patterns.why_it_works: The buyer keeps their place and compares colors on one view. The page stays about one product, and its address can be sent to someone with the color in it.
patterns.for_earf: Three EARF product pages already work this way. The Tropos page is headed 'Ember'; head it 'Tropos' and keep 'Color: Ember' as on the other three. Check that a swatch click keeps the gallery on the same view. One address per product with the tint in it. The pages /colors/<tint> and /tropos/<tint> are then spare: on 20 Nov, 0 of the visible links on the home page, the Tropos product page, /tropos, /mantle and /lighting led to either; point them at the product page.

patterns.pattern: 10. All finishes are shown together once under one light, and the swatch shows the material, not a flat color.
seen_at: Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360 (7 speakers in 7 finishes in one picture; square chips with the real texture)
Teenage Engineering: https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4 (8 tiles, one per color)
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3 (top views in each of 4 colors)
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 (3 squares of the veneer)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (swatches drawn as small horns)
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-evo-2/ (a wood-grain bar for the wood finish; staged photos each in another color)
Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers (one tile per color)
patterns.why_it_works: Choosing a color needs the colors side by side under the same light. A flat dot cannot show gloss, grain or how see-through a material is.
patterns.for_earf: EARF has 'All eight' rows for Hemisphere and Core and the grid of eight on /tropos. Add a row of eight for the Mantle and put the row of eight Tropos in the Tropos gallery. Replace the 8 flat dots with small renders of the same cast acrylic piece in each tint, since a tint's depth changes with thickness and light; Fog and Smoke gain most from this.

patterns.pattern: 11. Where there is no cart, the inquiry is a button with the weight of 'Add to cart', it appears more than once, it carries the choice made, and beside it stands what happens next.
seen_at: Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (configure, pick a dealer, 5-field form, 'Send request')
Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360 and https://www.linn.co.uk/us/try-linn (filled 'Book a demo'; 'Try Linn' in the header; says a specialist will be in touch)
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 (dealer finder in the buy area)
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3 (two dealer buttons, twice)
Pro-Ject: https://www.project-audio.com/en/product/debut-reference-10/ ('BUY LOCAL')
Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9 ('Experience in store', 'Book an appointment'; tick lines for delivery, trial, warranty)
OJAS: https://ojas.nyc/products/artbook-shelf-speaker-2 and https://ojas.nyc/products/klipsch-ko-r2 (lead time and the lot plan beside the button)
patterns.why_it_works: With no cart this is the page's only action; as a small text link it reads as an afterthought. Carrying the choice saves one exchange of letters. The made-to-order buyer's first questions are when and how; an answer at the button is what makes the letter worth writing.
patterns.for_earf: Today: two text links under the swatches, 'Ask about a pair' and 'Copy link', leading to a section with the address. Keep the letter; it needs no form. Make 'Ask about a pair' a filled button in the buy area and repeat it at the foot of the page. Have it open a letter to hello@earf.world with the subject and first line filled in from the page: product, tint, quantity ('Tropos, one pair, Ember'). Under it, two or three fact lines that only the owner can supply: who answers and how soon, the lead time, what happens after the quote. Put the status there too. Today it is a small label ('TROPOS 01 · IN DEVELOPMENT') and a footer line; OJAS puts 'Pre-Order' in the product's title and the plan beside the button. This is also what stands in for the removed 'Drawn to be made.' section: the stage and the dates, not a description of process.

patterns.pattern: 12. Words: one line that states a fact; numbers and names; the picture does the rest. A caption gives what cannot be seen: a name, a build, a place.
seen_at: OJAS: https://ojas.nyc/products/artbook-shelf-speaker-2 ("(these are made to order and have an 8 week lead time)")
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3 ("12 mm float glass opti-white polished platter")
U-Turn Audio: https://uturnaudio.com/products/orbit-custom ("($120) Solid walnut with satin finish.")
Teenage Engineering: https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4 and https://teenage.engineering/products/od-11 (caption names the house and its architect)
Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/turntables (caption bars name the product and build, not the scene)
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/heritage-premium-audio (sound as four drawn graphs)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 ("Sensitivity (1 Watt/1 m) > 109 dB"; "Recommended room size > 25 sqm")
patterns.why_it_works: A number or a name can be checked; an adjective cannot. The stores that describe sound without empty words give sensitivity, a range with its tolerance, a level at 1 m, a room size or a drawn curve, or they send the reader to a listening. The large brands (B&O, Sonos, KEF, Avantgarde) also use adjectives; the plain ones are the small makers.
patterns.for_earf: This is the owner's rule, and EARF's fact tables already follow it ('To about 51 Hz (-3 dB) before the room; to be measured on the first pair'). Where the site departs from the stores: the line under each color name on /tropos, /colors/<tint> and the Tropos product page ('The last light of the fire.', 'Glacier blue, and in no hurry.', 'Bottle green. Keep out of reach.'). In the stores the line under a finish name is a material or price fact, or there is none; EARF has that fact one line lower ('ACRYLIC Translucent red'). By the rule 'remove, do not rewrite', the eight lines go and the fact stays. When the first pair is measured, show the response as a drawn curve, as Klipsch does, and name where it can be heard.

patterns.pattern: 13. Specifications sit near the end, grouped under 4 to 7 plain headings, with sound given as measured figures and a sheet to download. Beside the picture stand one short paragraph and the button.
seen_at: Bang & Olufsen: https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9 (4 sections, 3 downloads; room size, SPL at 1 m, W x H x D)
Avantgarde Acoustic: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 (6 tabs, downloads)
KEF: https://us.kef.com/products/ls50-wireless-2 (table on the page, downloads)
Sonos: https://www.sonos.com/en-us/shop/era-300 (5 tabs)
Linn: https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360 (cards, 'Dimensions' card)
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-10 (table, manual PDF)
Teenage Engineering: https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4 (last block of the page)
Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 (spec sheet PDF)
patterns.why_it_works: The buyer who wants figures finds them all in one place; the buyer who does not is not stopped by a table at the top of the page.
patterns.for_earf: EARF's table of 10 to 13 ungrouped rows starts right beside the gallery, where 12 of the 13 stores put a paragraph and a button (OJAS is the exception). Keep every fact. Group them under Sound (drivers, amplifier, bass, loudness, inputs), Build (acrylic, cabinet, horn, lining), Size and weight, Care, and move the table below the gallery. Beside the gallery: one short paragraph, the price line, the swatches, the button. Add 'recommended room size' if the simulation supports a figure; B&O and Avantgarde both give one. Offer the same facts with the dimension drawing as a one-page PDF; 9 of the 13 offer a download.

patterns.pattern: 14. One page pattern for every product: the same blocks in the same order with the same heading rule.
seen_at: Klipsch: https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6 and https://www.klipsch.com/products/klipschorn-ak7
Rega: https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3 and https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-10

patterns.why_it_works: The visitor learns the page once. For the team a gap is visible at a glance: a product whose page lacks a block the others have.
patterns.for_earf: The four pages differ today: 5, 3, 9 and 4 pictures; one headed by a color and three by the product; 1.6 to 2.6 screens long, where 12 of the 13 stores run 5 to 24 screens (OJAS 1 to 2). Fix the order the stores share: gallery and buy area; one room picture; the parts view; all eight tints; specifications; the ask again. One picture and at most two lines per block. This order, the picture list of pattern 2 and the one-ground rule of pattern 1 are three checks a critic can run on every page before it goes live: count the pictures against the list, compare the grounds in every grid, and click every picture and marker to see that it lands on a product page.

merch.tile_ground_standard:
ONE RULE. Every product tile and every first picture is the product alone, whole and at rest, in one studio set. The set is the one the eight Tropos already stand in: a warm white sweep (about #E2DDD3 at the top and #F3F0E8 at mid-height, sampled from the home tile blue-hero.webp), one soft shadow to the lower right, an even margin, 4:5 upright. All four products, all eight tints.

At rest means: lamps switched off; the Mantle with its cover off and a record on. Each product at the angle that shows it whole: Tropos three-quarter at mid-height, Mantle three-quarter from above, the lamps level. The pendant hangs from the top edge of its tile on its cord. Tiles that share a row are the same size. The card under every tile is the page's own light color with dark text and the same lines: kind, name, one line, one button.

Where it applies: the family row and the color switcher on the home page, the two tiles on /lighting, the row of other products on each product page, the card a marker opens, and picture 1 of every product page, so that a click on a tile lands on the same picture, larger.

The lit lamp is picture 2 on its own page: the same camera and set, lamp on. A lamp's tile may change to that picture under the pointer; at rest every tile is off. The dark ground (today #1B1B1B to #252525) stays as a second ground with one job: lit and detail pictures inside a lamp's own gallery. It never appears in a tile, or anywhere two products stand side by side. On /lighting, where both tiles are lamps, one 'Night' switch may turn both to their lit pictures on the dark ground at once.

Why a light ground: the products are transparent and their tint is carried by light passing through to what is behind them. On the site's dark grounds the same tints go near-black: Hemisphere 'Off' on #2D2F31, and the Mantle's plinth in Ember, Poison, Ice, Haze and Smoke on its spot-lit gray.
Why lamps off: the family row and the switcher exist to show one tint across four products, and the lamps' unlit colors were matched to the others on purpose (owner, 17 Nov). Lit, an Ember lamp is salmon beside a deep red Tropos, and a Smoke lamp is pale gray beside a black one.
Why this set: the Tropos has its eight. The rule costs 24 renders (Mantle, Hemisphere and Core in eight tints), 16 more for the two lamps lit in the same frame, and 8 for the Mantle with its cover in the same frame.

Stores that do it, one light ground for every tile with lamps off:
- Design Within Reach: cut-outs on one light gray, lamps unlit, pendant cords run to the top of the tile (https://www.dwr.com/lighting-ceiling?lang=en_US).
- Fritz Hansen: one light gray square per lamp, pendants hung from the top edge, unlit; its related tiles hold a second picture for the pointer (https://fritzhansen.com/collections/lighting?filter.p.m.custom.show_on_plp_in_countries=US).
- Muuto: the page's warm light gray, cords to the top (https://www.muuto.com/products/lighting/pendant-lamps/).
- Hem: white, unlit, one tile per color; off then on as pictures 1 and 2 of Coco (https://hem.com/en-us/lighting ; https://hem.com/en-us/lighting/coco/30654).
- Louis Poulsen: 49 pendants unlit on #f6f6f6; a colored acrylic lamp lit, then unlit, in one frame (https://www.louispoulsen.com/en-us/c/indoor-lighting/pendants ; https://www.louispoulsen.com/en-us/c/indoor-lighting/portable-lamps/panthella-portable-lamp-the-originals).
- Bang & Olufsen: 31 tiles on one pale gray; its detail stills on a deep color are never mixed into the grid (https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers).
- Teenage Engineering: color tiles on light gray even on a black page (https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4).
- Bocci: one button turns every tile from day to night together (https://bocci.com/shop/28-series/).

The other choice seen is also one ground: every lamp lit on a mid-tone at Santa & Cole (https://www.santacole.com/en/pendant-lamps/), Gantri (https://www.gantri.com/shop/table-lights) and Tala (https://tala.co.uk/collections/portables), or lit on dark at Roll & Hill (https://www.rollandhill.com/collections/cloud). Taking it would mean re-rendering the Tropos set too, and the lit lamps would still not match the Tropos in tint. merch.hotspot_standard:
ONE RULE. A room picture leads to its products by name. A marker is a second way to the same place, never the only one.

Which pictures: room pictures only, meaning a product in a setting with other things (the bar pictures, the home rooms to come). Never a studio picture, a detail, a row of eight or a place picture. The home page's first picture carries the names row and no markers. Every other room picture carries both, on every page it appears on.

The names row: one line that names each product in the picture with the tint shown, each name a link to that product's page in that tint ('Tropos in Acid · Hemisphere in Ember · Core in Ember · Mantle in Ember'). Inside the bottom edge of the first picture; directly under the picture everywhere else. It is the picture's caption and there is no other.

How many markers: one per product kind in the frame, four at most. Where a kind appears more than once, mark the one that is whole and largest.

Where on the product: at the edge of its body where it meets plain background, the top edge first. One fixed spot per product on every picture: Tropos, the top rear corner of the cabinet; Mantle, a front corner of the plinth; Hemisphere, on the cord just above the cap; Core, the side of the base. Never on a driver, the mouth of the horn, a lit shade or ball, the record, the arm or a logo. Never within 44 px of another marker or a button.

What a marker shows: the first click or tap opens a small card beside it with the product's tile picture, its name, its kind, the tint shown and one arrow button ('See Tropos'). Nothing appears on hover that a tap cannot open. One marker style on the whole site.

Where it leads: the product's page in the tint shown, the same place as its name in the row.

Stores:
- Vitra marks every Inspirations picture on a product page: one white marker per product, set at the tip of the lamp's arm above the socket and not on the bulb; a click opens a card with the cut-out, the name, the designer and 'Buy'; a 'Products' button in the picture's corner backs the markers up; its home page has none (https://www.vitra.com/en-us/product/details/petite-potence).
- KEF marks the room pictures of its Blade collection page: one dot per speaker at the top edge of the cabinet against the plain wall; the card gives the name, an availability line, color dots and an arrow (https://us.kef.com/collections/blade-series).
- Names under the picture: HAY, a line of linked product names under each of 18 pictures (https://www.hay.com/inspiration/living-room-decoration); &Tradition, a caption that lists every product in the frame as links (https://www.andtradition.com/products/flowerpot-vp9); Flos, a caption link under each room picture and a '+' in the picture's corner that opens a card (https://flos.com/en/us/shop-by-room/dining-room/).
- On a home page's first picture: Gantri names the lamp in a chip at the lower left of its film (https://www.gantri.com/). None of the 35 stores the researchers opened puts markers there.
- A corner button that opens a list: Design Within Reach (https://www.dwr.com/), Herman Miller (https://store.hermanmiller.com/), Knoll (https://www.knoll.com/shop), Fritz Hansen (https://fritzhansen.com/).

Marks that explain parts are a different thing and look different: small numbers set in the ground beside the part on a plain picture, with one line per number (Avantgarde Trio G3: https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3 ; USM Haller: https://us.usm.com/pages/usm-haller-system). That is the one place a mark may sit next to a driver.
merch.page_structure:
HOME PAGE, in order.

1. Header. Keep.

2. First picture (the bar). Keep the picture, the headline and the line under it ('Horn speakers, lamps and a turntable, cast in tinted acrylic.' says what is sold). Change two things. 'Meet Tropos' goes to the Tropos page itself; today it lands on /tropos, a page with no gallery and no way to ask. Take the four dots off and put the names row inside the bottom edge (see the marker rule). Stores: one picture, three lines at most, one or two buttons at Vitra (https://www.vitra.com/en-us/home), Hem (https://hem.com/en-us) and Carl Hansen (https://www.carlhansen.com/en/en); Gantri names its first picture's lamp in a corner chip (https://www.gantri.com/).

3. The family, with the eight colors on it. Merge 'The family.' and 'Eight colors, the full spectrum.' into one section: the eight color chips, then one row of four equal tiles on the house ground, each with kind, name, one line and one button. A chip recolors all four tiles and their links. All four tiles lead to product pages. Reason: today the two sections show the same four products twice in a row, the second time without names, and the same Tropos picture is in both when the page loads. The line under the chips states the material the site already prints ('Ember. Translucent red') in place of the mood sentence. Add one picture of the acrylic itself: eight blocks side by side. Stores: a row of equal tiles with name and type at &Tradition (https://www.andtradition.com/), Louis Poulsen (https://www.louispoulsen.com/en-us), Lambert & Fils (https://lambertetfils.com/en-us) and Fritz Hansen's 'Discover our Icons' (https://fritzhansen.com/); one color choice that recolors every product at Gantri (https://www.gantri.com/shop/table-lights?colors=cobalt) and USM (https://us.usm.com/pages/usm-haller-system).

4. Add: a home by day. One wide picture of the listening room (two Tropos, the Mantle between them, a Core on the console), with the names row and markers. Reason: the only room on the site is a bar at night; a buyer for a home is shown no home. Stores: 'Get inspired by spaces' at Fritz Hansen (https://fritzhansen.com/); rooms by number of speakers at Syng (https://syngspace.com/); the first picture at U-Turn (https://uturnaudio.com/) and Transparent (https://transpa.rent/us/).

5. Each color is a place. Keep: it is EARF's own idea and no store has it. Each tile already leads to the Tropos in that tint. Label each tile 'Tropos in Ember', not 'Ember' alone: the name is the one thing the picture cannot say.

6. Write to us. Keep the letter. Add beside it what only the owner can supply (see the inquiry flow): what a letter brings back, how soon, the state of the build, who answers. The address becomes a button that opens the letter, with the address in text and a 'Copy' beside it. Stores: USM's custom-order paragraph and 'How to buy' (https://us.usm.com/pages/usm-haller-system); Linn's demo band (https://www.linn.co.uk/us).

7. Footer. Keep, with the render line.

Cut, and keep cut: 'Drawn to be made.' None of the ten furniture stores runs a text block about process on its home page, and the lighting stores show making with a picture (Tala's opened base, Carl Hansen's workshop photo). EARF's honest version is a real drawing from the CAD, on the product page.

PRODUCT PAGE, one pattern for all four, in order.

1. Pictures and the buy area. Pictures at the left in two thirds of the width, large (today the stage is 520 px in a 1440 window; the six the audio researcher measured are 612 to 803 px), each opening larger on a click, picture 1 the product alone on the house ground. The buy area at the right stays in view while the pictures scroll and holds: the kind and status line; the product's name as the title on all four pages (Tropos, not Ember); the color as the second line, with chips that show the acrylic and the chosen name printed; one paragraph on what it is, what it is made of and how it is used (the words exist on /mantle, /lighting and /tropos); the ask button with its three fact lines; the render line. A color change keeps the picture the visitor is on. Stores: the buy column stays in view at Flos Bellhop (https://flos.com/en/us/bellhop-unplugged/M-bellhop-unplugged.html), Muuto Ambit (https://www.muuto.com/product/Ambit-Pendant-Lamp/), Carl Hansen RF200 (https://www.carlhansen.com/en/en/collection/lighting/table-lamps/rf200) and Apparatus (https://apparatusstudio.com/products/pip-arrow); a paragraph above the facts at HAY (105 words), DWR (85) and Muuto (60); no store opened heads a product page with a color.

2. The room, large, with the names row and markers. Stores: Hem 'Featured images' (https://hem.com/en-us/lighting/coco/30654); Vitra 'Inspirations' (https://www.vitra.com/en-us/product/details/petite-potence).

3. The parts, named: one plain picture with numbers and the matching lines. Hemisphere has it ('How it lights'); Tropos, Mantle and Core get theirs. Stores: Avantgarde 'Highlights' (https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3); USM (https://us.usm.com/pages/usm-haller-system); Klipsch's labeled cutaway (https://www.klipsch.com/products/la-scala-al6).

4. All eight, in one row at full width, each a link to that tint. Stores: Flos Bellhop picture 5; Linn 360 (https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360); Teenage Engineering OB-4 (https://teenage.engineering/products/ob-4).

5. Specifications, under four or five plain headings, one fact to a row, inches beside millimeters and pounds beside kilograms, the drawing beside them, one page to download. Stores: Bang & Olufsen, four sections and three downloads (https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9); Fritz Hansen, centimeters and inches side by side (https://fritzhansen.com/products/caravaggio-pendant-p2-caravaggiop2); Lindsey Adelman, inches and centimeters and a tear sheet (https://lindseyadelman.com/ps0102); Allied Maker, one fact per block and a cut sheet (https://www.alliedmaker.com/Dome-Pendant-14-Perforated).

6. The rest of the family: the other three products as tiles in the tint now chosen. It replaces the text lines at the foot of the pages ('Also in Lighting: Core...', 'Pair it with Tropos.'). Stores: &Tradition, 12 family icons on every product page (https://www.andtradition.com/products/flowerpot-vp9); HAY '/ FAMILY' (https://www.hay.com/hay/lighting/table-lamp/pc-portable-lamp); Roll & Hill 'Complete the collection' (https://www.rollandhill.com/products/cloud-pendant-14).

7. The ask again. On a phone the ask is a bar fixed to the bottom of the screen. Stores: Rega, the dealer buttons mid-page and again at the end (https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3); Flos, Gantri, Sonos and Anglepoise keep the action in a bar at the bottom.

Cut from the product page: 'Copy link' as a text link of the same weight as the ask (a small icon instead); the mood sentence that stands as the Tropos page's only line; the facts table as the main text beside the pictures.

COLOR PAGES (/colors/<tint>). Retire them. Each shows one of the four products, a place picture that is not a link, a flat disc and the mood sentence, and none of the links I listed on the home page, the header pages or the product pages leads to them. No store has a page for a color: a color lives inside the product page and in the listing (Hem, HAY, USM, DWR, Vitra). Send each address to the home family row with that tint chosen; until that row has an address per tint, to the Tropos page in that tint.

THE THREE HEADER PAGES.
/tropos: fold into the Tropos product page. Today it is a step between the home page and the product: eight cards to pick a color from, then 'The particulars'. The header's 'Tropos', the first picture's 'Meet Tropos' and the family tile all land there, while the other three family tiles land on product pages. The eight cards become block 4 of the product page; 'The particulars' (15 rows) becomes its specifications. Send /tropos to the product page.
/mantle: fold into the Mantle product page. It is one picture, one paragraph and a link to the product page that opens with the same picture. Its 40-word paragraph becomes the product page's paragraph in place of 'A turntable in cast acrylic.' Send /mantle to the product page.
/lighting: keep as the one listing, rebuilt: the title, one room picture, then two equal tiles on the house ground (Hemisphere, Core) with kind, name, line, chips and button on the first screen. Today the names and links sit under four pictures at the foot of the page and the two bar pictures lead nowhere. The 'Cordless.' paragraph is about the Core alone and moves to the Core page. Stores: the DWR and Knoll listings open with the title and one room picture, then the grid (https://www.dwr.com/lighting-portable-lamps?lang=en_US ; https://www.knoll.com/shop/en_us/living-side-coffee-tables).

HOW I LOOKED. The live site on 20 Nov 2026 between 08:50 and 09:25 UTC, Chromium through Playwright at 1440 x 900 and as a 390 x 844 phone, device scale 1: fresh slices of every page, every thumbnail of all 32 product pages clicked, the ask, the markers, the switcher and the color chips clicked. The pack's own slices were taken before the 20 Nov fixes and are not used for the findings. Other stores: I looked at the researchers' saved screens for DWR, Louis Poulsen, Flos, Gantri, Santa & Cole, Roll & Hill, Vitra, KEF, Klipsch, Transparent, OJAS and Avantgarde, and opened four more myself (OMA, Apparatus, Lindsey Adelman, Allied Maker). Every other statement about a store is taken from the three researchers' findings. I did not send mail and did not test other browsers. Files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/ (live/ = the site, gal/ = gallery logs and pictures, ref/ = the four stores, the .js files = the checks).
merch.inquiry_flow:
The path from wanting to asking, in order.

0. The address has to work. On 20 Nov at about 09:25 UTC a lookup of earf.world returned name servers and no mail record. I did not send a test letter. Until mail is set up, a letter to hello@earf.world has nowhere to go.

1. One action per product page, with the weight of a buy button. A filled button in the buy area ('Ask about a pair' for Tropos; 'Ask about Mantle', 'Ask about Hemisphere', 'Ask about Core'), in view while the pictures scroll, again at the end of the page, and as a bar at the bottom of the screen on a phone. 'Copy link' becomes a small icon. Seen: Apparatus, one 'INQUIRE' button in the column that stays in view (https://apparatusstudio.com/products/pip-arrow); Lindsey Adelman, 'Inquire about this model' (https://lindseyadelman.com/ps0102); Linn, a filled 'Book a demo' on the product and 'Try Linn' in the header of every page (https://www.linn.co.uk/us/speakers/360); Rega, the two dealer buttons mid-page and again at the end (https://www.rega.co.uk/products/planar-3).

2. The ask opens where the visitor is. Today it leaves the product page for the bottom of the home page. Apparatus and Lindsey Adelman open a small panel over the product page; Avantgarde's request form is the last step of the configurator on its product page (https://avantgarde-acoustic.de/en/products/trio-g3).

3. The choice travels with it. The letter opens with its subject and first line filled in from the page: 'Tropos, one pair, in Ember'. Seen: Lindsey Adelman's panel arrives with the product ('PS.01.02 Swag Sconce'), the colorway and a first line ('Hello, I'm interested in the PS.01.02 Swag Sconce.') filled in; Apparatus fills the subject ('APPARATUS INQUIRY : ARROW') and the message; Avantgarde carries the chosen colors to the dealer; Hem writes the choice into the page address (https://hem.com/en-us/lighting/alphabeta?top=13316&bottom=13314&base=13337). EARF keeps its letter: a mail link with subject and body, and the address shown in text beside it with a 'Copy' for visitors whose computer has no mail program. A three-field panel (email, where it ships, message) that sends the same letter is the stronger form and is what both studios use.

4. Three facts beside the button, all from the owner, none invented. What comes back: a quote for the pair delivered and a build slot. How soon: Apparatus prints 'WE WILL REPLY WITHIN TWO BUSINESS DAYS.'; Lindsey Adelman 'We will reply within 1 business day.' How long a build takes, or, while there is no build time, the true state of things in its place. Seen, the wait next to the action: Lindsey Adelman '$10,500 / 24 Weeks' on every colorway; Apparatus 'APPROXIMATELY 12-14 WEEKS UNLESS OTHERWISE QUOTED'; Allied Maker 'LEAD TIME 10 - 12 weeks' (https://www.alliedmaker.com/Dome-Pendant-14-Perforated); OJAS '(these are made to order and have an 8 week lead time)' (https://ojas.nyc/products/artbook-shelf-speaker-2); Vitra '7-8 weeks', changing with the color (https://www.vitra.com/en-us/product/details/petite-potence); USM 'Custom designs are ready to ship in 14-16 weeks.' (https://us.usm.com/pages/usm-haller-system).

5. A price to start from, when the owner has one. The makers here who sell by inquiry print one: Apparatus 'PRICE FROM : $5600', Lindsey Adelman '$10,500', Allied Maker '$1,900.00 +', Roll & Hill 'STARTING FROM $4,820' (https://www.rollandhill.com/products/cloud-pendant-14), Linn 'From US$95,915'. The ones that print none send the buyer to a dealer who quotes (HAY, &Tradition, Santa & Cole, Carl Hansen, Rega, Klipsch Heritage, Avantgarde). EARF has no dealer, so 'Price on request' alone leaves the visitor unable to tell whether to write at all.

6. What happens after the letter, as steps with times, next to 'Write to us.': you write (product, tint, where it ships); we quote; we build; it ships. With them, what a buyer of an unbuilt, made-to-order object needs before writing and the site says nowhere: who builds it and where, the warranty, how it ships, what happens if it arrives damaged. Seen: OJAS gives the buyer a lot number and a run of updates (horns received, crossovers built, cabinets, assembly, testing, shipping, setup) and says 'Our goal is for you to know as much as we do about the status of your speaker build.'; Bang & Olufsen's tick lines under the button for delivery, trial and warranty (https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9); USM's footer heading 'HOW TO BUY'. This is also where the content of the removed 'Drawn to be made.' belongs: as stages and dates, not as a description.

7. A second door for the trade, and a smaller step for everyone else. The site names 'designers, dealers and press': give them the one-page sheet and the drawing (Lindsey Adelman: 'Request CAD files' and a tear sheet; Apparatus: 'VIEW TEAR SHEET' and 'TRADE APPLICATION'; Muuto: 'Are you a Professional or Retailer?'). For the visitor who is not ready to write: one field, 'Tell me when the first pair is built' (Tala: 'NOTIFY ME WHEN AVAILABLE'; OJAS: 'Notify me when back in stock'). Acrylic chips by mail are the owner's call (Roll & Hill sells sample chips of its metals at $12).

findings.where: Home page, 'The family.' and the color switcher under 'Eight colors, the full spectrum.' (https://www.earf.world/)
findings.what: Four product pictures stand on three grounds, in three tile sizes, over two card colors. Tropos: warm white (#E2DDD3 to #F3F0E8). Mantle: a spot-lit gray with dark upper corners (#2C2825 at the corner, #CFCDC9 at mid-height). Hemisphere and Core: lit, on near-black (#1B1B1B to #252525). At 1440 wide the tiles are 696 x 1219, 696 x 653 and two of 340 x 551; the lamps' text panels are dark, the other two light. This is the owner's first point; the Mantle's ground is a third one he did not name.
findings.why_it_matters: Side by side, the eye compares the grounds and not the products. The two dark tiles read as another kind of thing or as a mistake.
findings.fix: The tile ground rule: render Mantle, Hemisphere and Core in the Tropos set in all eight tints (24 pictures), lamps off; four equal tiles in one row; one light card.
findings.evidence: Colors sampled from blue-hero.webp, mantle-ember.webp, home-hemisphere-haze.webp and home-core-poison.webp; sizes read from the page. Live site, 20 Nov 2026, 08:50 UTC. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/live/home-d-02.jpg, home-d-03.jpg, home-dom-d.json

findings.where: Home page, color switcher, all eight colors
findings.what: One chosen color appears as three or four colors. Ember: a deep red Tropos, a near-black Mantle with one red corner, a salmon Hemisphere and a coral Core, both lit. Smoke: a black Tropos and Mantle beside two pale gray lamps. Fog: a clear Tropos beside a mid-gray Mantle. Between Poison, Ice, Haze and Smoke the Mantle picture hardly changes.
findings.why_it_matters: The switcher's one job is to show a tint across the family. A lit lamp shows the color of its glow, not of its acrylic, and the Mantle's plinth is too dark to carry its tint. A buyer cannot tell what 'Ember' is.
findings.fix: Lamps off on the house ground in the switcher and the family row (their unlit colors were matched to the Tropos); the glow becomes picture 2 on the lamp pages; light the Mantle so the plinth carries its tint.

findings.where: All four product pages, every tint (live, 20 Nov, 08:54 to 08:58 UTC)
findings.what: Picture counts. Tropos: 5 in seven tints, 6 in Acid. Hemisphere: 9 in Ember, 5 in Dust and Acid, 4 in Poison, Ice, Haze, Fog and Smoke. Core: 4 in Ember and Dust, 3 in the other six, and two of those three are rows of all eight, so one picture of the lamp itself. Mantle: 3 in Ember, 2 in the other seven. Hemisphere's 'Off', 'The cap', 'The rim' and 'Over a table' exist in Ember only. The stores' sets run from 6 to 32 pictures. This is the owner's second point.
findings.why_it_matters: A buyer who picks Core in Ice or Mantle in Haze has one or two pictures to decide on, and fewer than the buyer who picks Ember.
findings.fix: Render to the four picture lists in this report, the same list in every tint; where a picture is shared by all tints, show it on all eight pages.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/gal/log-speaker.txt, log-hemisphere.txt, log-core.txt, log-mantle.txt (every thumbnail of all 32 pages clicked)

findings.where: Whole site
findings.what: No product is shown in a home and no room is shown by day. The one room is a bar at night: the home page's first picture, 'At the bar' on seven product pages, two pictures on /lighting. Hemisphere's 'Over a table' (Ember only) is a table in a room with no walls, the lamp about a tenth of the frame's width. No picture shows a pair of Tropos in a living room, the Mantle on furniture at home, or the Core beside anything of known size.
findings.why_it_matters: A 1295 mm, 73 kg loudspeaker, a 160 mm lamp and a 200 mm pendant are bought for rooms. Nothing tells a buyer how big they are next to a sofa, a table or a book, or how they look in daylight.
findings.fix: Four scenes: a listening room by day with two cameras (the pair of Tropos; the Mantle on the console); a small dining table by day and in the evening (Hemisphere); a shelf or bedside table by day and in the evening (Core); a terrace table at dusk (Core). Furniture at true size, cables in frame, no people.
findings.evidence: Design Within Reach shows the Panthella Portable in place in 16 of 17 pictures; OMA opens its AC1 page with a pair in a listening room (https://oswaldsmillaudio.com/ac1). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/ref/oma/oma-ac1-sheet-01.jpg

findings.where: Tropos product pages (https://www.earf.world/tropos/ember and the other seven)
findings.what: The page opens on the landscape ('Out'), where the speaker is about a quarter of the frame's width in a dark scene; the plain picture ('Front') is second. The title is the color ('Ember', 64 px); 'Tropos' stands only in the small label 'TROPOS 01 · IN DEVELOPMENT' and in the breadcrumb. The one line under the title is about the color ('The last light of the fire.'); no sentence on the page says what the product is, though the home tile has one ('A powered horn loudspeaker in cast acrylic.'). On a 390 px phone the first screen is a dark landscape titled 'Ember'. The other three pages are titled by product and open on the product.
findings.why_it_matters: A visitor who arrives by a shared link cannot tell what is for sale or what it looks like.
findings.fix: 'Front' first and the landscape late in the set; the title 'Tropos' with 'Color: Ember' as the second line, as on the other three pages; the home tile's line and the two sentences on /tropos as the paragraph.

findings.where: Every product page; /contact
findings.what: The way to buy is an underlined 18 px text link ('Ask about a pair', 'Ask about it') beside 'Copy link' in the same style. It appears once. On a phone it is on the second screen (1,002 px down on Tropos, 1,047 px on Hemisphere) and scrolls away. A click leaves the product page for the bottom of the home page ('Write to us.', 4,426 px down a 5,326 px page). The mail link there is mailto:hello@earf.world with no subject, so the product and tint the visitor chose are gone. Nothing says what a letter brings back, how soon, or how long a build takes.
findings.why_it_matters: With no cart this link is the store. As built it is the least visible control on the page, it drops what the visitor chose, and it asks for a letter without saying what the letter will get.
findings.fix: Inquiry flow, steps 1 to 4: a filled button in a buy area that stays in view, repeated at the foot and as a bottom bar on a phone; it opens in place; the letter starts with 'Tropos, one pair, in Ember'; three fact lines from the owner under it.
findings.evidence: Tested on Tropos in Ice, Hemisphere in Haze, Core in Poison (phone), Mantle in Dust (phone). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/live/ask-speaker-ice-d.jpg; ask.js

findings.where: hello@earf.world, the only way to buy
findings.what: The domain earf.world had name servers and no mail record on 20 Nov at about 09:25 UTC (dns.google: NS ns1 and ns2.vercel-dns.com; MX none). I did not send a test letter.
findings.why_it_matters: A letter written today has nowhere to go. The buyer gets silence or a bounce days later, and the site offers no other route: no form, phone or dealer.
findings.fix: Set up mail for the address before any other work on the ask. Then send a letter from an outside account and answer it.
findings.evidence: Lookup with a control lookup of another domain in the same run.

findings.where: Product pages ('Price on request.') and 'Write to us.'
findings.what: No price to start from, and no word on lead time, reply time, warranty, shipping or returns. In the visible text of all 47 pages (the copy pass's dump, 281 lines) the only statements are 'Everything is made to order, so we quote rather than list. findings.where: The site's only way to buy or ask: the mail link a.mail (mailto:hello@earf.world) in "Write to us." on / and /contact, reached from every "Ask about ..." link and from Contact in the header and footer.
findings.what: The domain earf.world has no mail record. Looked up at dns.google on 20 Nov at about 08:15 UTC: MX for earf.world returned no answer (status NOERROR, only the SOA line); TXT returned none; NS returned ns1.vercel-dns.com and ns2.vercel-dns.com; a control lookup (MX for gmail.com) answered normally. With no MX record a sending server falls back to the domain's A records, 216.198.79.65 and 216.198.79.1, which are the web host. findings.fix: Set up mail for earf.world (MX and SPF records) before any other work on the buy path, then send a test from an outside account and confirm it arrives. Until it does, show an address that works. Add "a test letter arrives" to the checks run before each publish.

findings.fix: Site: let the stage take each picture's shape, as it already does for Mantle, or cut 4:5 versions from the existing files where the content allows (bar and table scenes). Render lanes: 4:5 group pictures (two rows of four) to replace the 3:1 rows in the gallery.

findings.where: Lamp pictures on near-black: home-hemisphere-<tint>.webp and home-core-<tint>.webp (800 x 800, home tiles); hemisphere-<tint>.webp, core-<tint>.webp, hemisphere-<tint>-under.webp (1200 x 1500, 'Lit' and 'From below').
findings.what: The files are very small: 3.4 to 7.3 kB at 800 x 800 and 6.8 to 13.3 kB for 'Lit' at 1200 x 1500, which is 0.03 to 0.09 bits per pixel (the Tropos tile has 0.28, the place pictures 0.5 to 1.4). The dark ground is stored as 9 to 15 gray levels (27 to 36 of 255 in home-hemisphere-haze) in flat, block-shaped steps with no grain (0.3 to 0.6 levels). Flat runs reach 393 px of 800 in home-hemisphere-haze, 560 px in home-core-poison and the full 1200 px in core-smoke. Brightened 3 to 4 times the ground breaks into stair steps and mottled blocks; at normal brightness I saw faint mottling in a 2x screenshot of the 'Lit' stage.
findings.why_it_matters: Smooth dark grounds are where banding shows first, on bright phone screens and in dark rooms, and a blotchy ground makes a render look like a render.
findings.fix: Site: re-encode these from the masters at a much higher quality (or lossless) and add fine grain before encoding so the steps break up. No new render.
findings.verdict_evidence: Weights: home-hemisphere 3,450 to 5,890 bytes and home-core 4,398 to 7,514 bytes at 800 x 800; hemisphere-<tint>.webp 6,968 to 12,136 and core-<tint>.webp 8,108 to 13,624 at 1200 x 1500: 0.031 to 0.094 bits per pixel; blue-hero 0.285; place pictures 0.46 to 1.37. In home-hemisphere-haze 99% of the ground sits on 8 gray levels, 27 to 35 (the critic has 9 to 15 and 27 to 36); other files 8 to 13, Core in Acid 19, Core in Fog 25. Longest run of one value along a row: 393 px in home-hemisphere-haze, 560 px in home-core-poison, 1200 px in core-smoke. Grain by my measure is 0.05 to 0.17 levels in these files against 0.6 to 1.5 in the place pictures (the critic's 0.3 to 0.6 is a different measure). Brightened four times, home-hemisphere-haze breaks into blocks and stair steps. I did not repeat the 2x screenshot. Not in the finding: the same holds for core-row.webp (0.11 bits per pixel, 8 levels, runs of 980 px), hemisphere-row.webp (0.07, runs of 864 px) and core-row-day.webp (0.09, 5 levels, runs of 1200 px).

findings.where: Product pages, gallery; Tropos 'Turning'.
findings.what: The view names ('Out', 'Front', 'The amplifier', 'Horn, behind', 'Turning', 'Lit', 'Off', 'By day' and the rest) exist only as hidden labels for screen readers; the buttons have no title and no text. findings.where: Product pages: the facts lists against the galleries
findings.what: Things the text states and no picture shows. Core: the dock, the touch ring, the three cells 'you can replace yourself', use on a terrace. Hemisphere: the quarter-turn change of shade ('Shades: In all eight colors, sold singly'), the 150 mm canopy, the cord. Mantle: the arm (Rega RB330), the phono stage's sockets and bypass switch, the view from above. Tropos: the whole back, the sides.
findings.why_it_matters: A claim with nothing to look at is taken on trust. These are also the parts a buyer handles.
findings.fix: The pictures in the four sets: dock and ring, shade off its fitting, arm close-up, back views, top view. Draw only what is in the CAD.
findings.evidence: Facts from D.json and the live pages; galleries as logged in gal/.
findings.verdict_evidence: Facts on the pages: Core 'Touch the ring: tap to switch, hold to dim'; 'it charges in two to three hours on its dock, on three standard LiFePO4 cells you can replace yourself'; 'Designed to meet IP44, for terraces and spilled drinks'. Hemisphere 'with a quarter-turn catch'; 'a canopy of satin black anodized aluminum, 150 mm across'; 'Shades: In all eight colors, sold singly'. Mantle 'Arm: Rega RB330'; 'Built in, for moving-magnet cartridges, with a line out and a switch to bypass it'. No gallery picture shows the dock, the ring as a control, the cells, a terrace, a shade off its fitting, the canopy, the Mantle's sockets or switch, the Mantle from above, the Tropos's whole back or its sides.
findings.correction: Two things on the list are in the pictures, though with no close view. findings.where: Facts lists on every product page and 'The particulars' on /tropos
findings.what: Sizes in millimeters and weights in kilograms only ('1295 high, 560 wide, 428 deep (mm)', 'About 73 kg (modeled)', '200 mm across', '160 mm ball, 180 mm tall', '450 wide, 360 deep, 161 high'), on a site in American English whose pendant runs on '120 V'. No drawing on any page and no sheet to download.
findings.why_it_matters: An American buyer thinks in inches and pounds. A row of numbers does not say which number is which, and a designer or dealer has nothing to pass on.
findings.fix: Inches beside millimeters and pounds beside kilograms (Tropos about 51 x 22 x 16 7/8 in and 161 lb); one line drawing per product from the CAD; one page per product to download.
findings.evidence: Fritz Hansen gives centimeters and inches side by side (https://fritzhansen.com/products/caravaggio-pendant-p2-caravaggiop2); Lindsey Adelman 'H 21in / 53cm ... WT 10lb / 5kg' and a tear sheet (https://lindseyadelman.com/ps0102).
findings.verdict_evidence: Facts as shown: '1295 high, 560 wide, 428 deep (mm)'; 'About 73 kg (modeled)'; '200 mm across'; '160 mm ball, 180 mm tall'; '450 wide, 360 deep, 161 high to the top of the arm; 196 high with the cover on (mm)'; 'About 1.5 kg'; 'About 11.6 kg; about 12.7 kg with the cover'; '120 V, dimmable'. Inches appear only for the drivers ('15-inch woofer', '2-inch compression driver'). The source has no 'lb', no drawing, no download and no PDF. Fritz Hansen's page gives 33.7 cm and 25.8 cm, then 13.2 in and 10.1 in. Lindsey Adelman's gives 'H 21in / 53cm', 'WT 10lb / 5kg' and a tear sheet. Judgment: 'thinks in inches and pounds'.

findings.where: Mantle: home tile, switcher cell and picture 1 ('In the studio'), all tints

The front and right parts of the plinth are L* 12 to 24 with chroma 5 to 9 in every hue. 'With its cover' shows the tint across the cover in all eight.

findings.where: Product pages, the gallery
findings.what: The stage is 520 x 650 px in a 1440 px window, 36 percent of the width. Wide pictures shrink to fit: the bar at 520 x 292, the rows of eight at 520 x 173 with each lamp about 35 px across. A click on the picture does nothing; there is no larger view. Hemisphere's nine thumbnails do not fit their strip: 12 px of the ninth shows at 1440, and five and a half show on a 390 px phone. Under the gallery the left half of the page is empty, about 800 px on the Mantle page.
findings.why_it_matters: For a product nobody can see built, the pictures are the product. Here they are small, and the widest ones are the smallest.
findings.fix: Pictures in two thirds of the page width, stacked or on a stage of 700 px or more; a click opens the full file; every thumbnail visible; rooms and rows at full width under the gallery.
findings.verdict_evidence: Stage 520 x 650 in a 1440 window, 36% of the width. Bar 520 x 292. Rows 520 x 173; Core balls 36 to 37 px, Hemisphere shades 42 to 47 px. A click and a double click on the picture on three pages changed nothing: no dialog, no new element, no new tab. Hemisphere in Ember: 12 of 56 px of the ninth thumbnail at 1440; five thumbnails and 42 of 56 px of the sixth at 390. The left column below the gallery is empty for 821 px on Mantle, 437 px on Core, 400 px on Hemisphere and 254 px on Tropos. Judgment: 'the pictures are the product'.

findings.where: Tropos pages, 'Turning'
findings.what: The turn shows the horn alone, not the speaker. Its frames are 640 x 576 on a ground tinted to each color (#E0CCC7 on the Ember page and #C4DBE5 on Ice, by the page's own data), next to stills of 1000 x 1250 on warm white. It plays once when chosen and then follows a drag; the only cue is a ring with two arrows that replaces the pointer on a computer.
findings.why_it_matters: The back and sides of a 73 kg object that stands in the open are what a turn is for, and they are not in it. A phone user gets no cue that it turns.
findings.fix: Keep the horn turn, as the owner asked. When it is next rendered: the whole speaker, the house ground, stage size, a visible '360' label, started by the visitor.

The page data's first color is #E0CCC7 for Ember and #C4DBE5 for Ice; the stage fill is #E2CFCA and #C7DFE7. 'Front' is 1000 x 1250 on warm white. It turned once on opening and then followed a drag. The cue is the pointer ring with two chevrons, on a computer only. On an emulated phone it also turned once and followed a swipe, with no cue.

findings.where: Product pages, right column
findings.what: The longest text beside the pictures is the facts table: 10 to 15 rows, open, ungrouped. Single cells hold several facts (Hemisphere 'Light': lumens, lux, CRI, what glows and four color temperatures, 65 words). Above it stands one line; on the Mantle page it is five words ('A turntable in cast acrylic.') while /mantle holds a 40-word paragraph and the home tile a third wording. Tropos's facts exist twice in two lengths: 10 rows on the product page, 15 on /tropos.
findings.why_it_matters: A buyer looking for one number reads cells of prose; a buyer who wants to know what the thing is gets a table.
findings.fix: One short paragraph by the title, from words the site already has; the facts lower on the page under four or five headings, one fact to a row, one list per product.
findings.evidence: Tala and Bocci set one fact per line ('Lumens: 200'; 'CCT — 2500K'); Bang & Olufsen groups under SOUND, DESIGN, POWER, CONNECTIVITY (https://www.bang-olufsen.com/en/us/speakers/beosound-a9).
findings.verdict_evidence: Rows: Tropos 10, Hemisphere 10, Core 12, Mantle 15, in one open list each. Hemisphere 'Light' is 65 words. Mantle product line: 'A turntable in cast acrylic.' (five words). Home tile: 'A turntable on a floating acrylic plinth.' Tropos: 10 rows on the product page, 15 under 'The particulars' on /tropos. Tala sets 'Lumens: 200' on a line of its own; Bocci 'CCT — 2500K'. I could not confirm Bang & Olufsen's four headings: the page did not finish loading.
findings.correction: The paragraph on /mantle is 34 words, not 40: 'A turntable in the speakers' acrylic. Its tinted plinth floats 40 mm over a smoked base on four black posts. The motor is fixed under the plinth, and the phono stage is built in.'

findings.where: Foot of each product page
findings.what: The other products appear as one line of text. Hemisphere: 'Also in Lighting: Core, a table lamp in the same eight.' Core: the reverse. Mantle: 'Pair it with Tropos.', which leads to the list of eight and not to a product page. The Tropos page links to none of the other three.
findings.why_it_matters: The buyer of one piece is not shown the others, and the one thing only EARF has, the same eight tints across four products, cannot be seen from a product page.
findings.fix: A row of the other three products as tiles in the tint now chosen, each a link to that product in that tint. No new pictures once the tile set exists.
findings.verdict_evidence: Foot lines. Hemisphere: 'Also in Lighting: Core, a table lamp in the same eight.' (to #core-ember whatever tint is open). Core: 'Also in Lighting: Hemisphere, a pendant in the same eight.' Mantle: 'Pair it with Tropos.' (to /tropos). Tropos: 'More on the speaker: the particulars.' (to the table on /tropos). No product page shows a tile of another product. Judgment: 'cannot be seen from a product page'.

findings.where: Color chips on every page
findings.what: The eight chips are flat dots of one color. Fog, which is clear, is a white dot; Smoke is a dark gray dot. No picture on the site shows the acrylic by itself.
findings.why_it_matters: A flat dot cannot show a transparent material, its depth or how it takes light, and that material is what the buyer is choosing.
findings.fix: Eight small renders of one acrylic block in each tint on the house ground as the chips; one picture of the eight blocks side by side for the home color row and the product pages.
findings.evidence: Lambert & Fils uses swatches of the finish's own texture and a 'Material library' (https://lambertetfils.com/en-us/products/parc-04); Bocci uses photo swatches of the glass (https://bocci.com/shop/products/14p/); Lindsey Adelman pairs a metal chip and a glass chip per colorway (https://lindseyadelman.com/ps0102).
findings.verdict_evidence: The chips are spans with one background color and no picture: Ember rgb(181, 4, 4), Dust rgb(211, 93, 23), Acid rgb(197, 188, 30), Poison rgb(2, 118, 20), Ice rgb(17, 105, 193), Haze rgb(80, 12, 180), Fog rgb(246, 248, 248), Smoke rgb(52, 50, 58). None of the 265 files is a picture of the material alone. Lambert & Fils shows square finish chips and 'Material library'. Lindsey Adelman shows a metal chip and a glass chip for each colorway. On Bocci I confirmed 'COLOUR OPTIONS' and did not look at the swatches. Judgment: 'cannot show a transparent material'.

findings.where: Whole site
findings.what: Nothing says who EARF is: no name, no workshop, no page about the maker. 'Designed in San Francisco.' in the footer is the only such statement.
findings.why_it_matters: The site asks a stranger to write a letter about an object that is not built yet, at a price not stated.
findings.fix: Next to 'Write to us.': who answers, where the work is done, what is finished and what comes next. Facts from the owner, in two or three lines.
findings.evidence: OJAS opens its home page with a paragraph about the maker (https://ojas.nyc/); Allied Maker prints 'Handmade in USA' beside the price (https://www.alliedmaker.com/Dome-Pendant-14-Perforated); USM closes its facts with 'Made in Switzerland.' (https://us.usm.com/products/usm-haller-nightstand-p).
findings.verdict_evidence: The visible text has no person's name and no 'about', 'workshop' or 'founder'. 'Designed in San Francisco.' is in the footer. OJAS opens its home page with a paragraph on its maker; Allied Maker has 'Handmade in USA'; USM has 'Made in Switzerland'. The rest is judgment.

findings.where: Footer; the small label over each product title; the end of the facts
findings.what: 'Pictures are renders until the first pair is built.' stands in the footer only. 'IN DEVELOPMENT' is a small label over the title with no word on what it means for ordering. 'Design figures; they may change before production' is the second-last row of the facts.
findings.why_it_matters: The buyer should meet the limit where they look at the picture and where they decide to write, not at the foot of the page.
findings.fix: The render line in small type under the gallery on every product page, and the status with its meaning beside the ask. Keep the footer line.
findings.evidence: Artemide prints its color note directly under its 3D view (https://www.artemide.com/en/subfamily/23264/nessino); OJAS puts 'Pre-Order' in the product's title.
findings.verdict_evidence: 'Pictures are renders until the first pair is built.' is in the footer and nowhere else. The label reads 'TROPOS 01 · IN DEVELOPMENT', 'LIGHTING · PENDANT · IN DEVELOPMENT', 'LIGHTING · TABLE LAMP · IN DEVELOPMENT', 'MANTLE · IN DEVELOPMENT' at 13 px. 'Figures: Design figures; they may change before production' is the second-last row on the Hemisphere, Core and Mantle pages. Artemide's page has 'The colors represented in the 3D model above do not exactly match the real colors of the product.' OJAS has a product titled Klipsch/OJAS kO-R2 'Pre-Order'.
findings.correction: The eight Tropos product pages have no 'Figures' row; their list ends with 'Care'. For Tropos the line is on /tropos only, last of 15 rows, in other words: 'Design figures, from the drawings and their simulation; measured ones follow with the first pair'.

findings.where: Home page, 'Each color is a place.'
findings.what: Since 20 Nov each tile leads to the Tropos in that tint: the owner's third point is fixed. Two things remain. The label is the color alone ('Ember'), so nothing says the object is a Tropos or that the tile leads to it. And the page it leads to opens on the same landscape, so the click shows the same picture again.
findings.why_it_matters: A visitor who clicks a picture of a thing wants that thing, shown plainly.
findings.fix: Label each tile 'Tropos in Ember'. With 'Front' as picture 1 the click lands on the plain view.
findings.verdict_evidence: Clicked tiles 1, 5 and 8: links #speaker-ember, #speaker-ice, #speaker-smoke, landing on /tropos/<tint>. The label is the color name alone at 16 px. Each page opens on 'Out', the same file as the tile, under the title 'Ember', 'Ice', 'Smoke'. Judgment: what a visitor wants.

findings.where: Core in Dust, 'At the bar'
findings.what: The picture is the pendants picture (bar-pendants.webp): five Hemispheres fill the frame and the Dust Core is at the bottom edge. Core in Ember has its own close view at the bar; the other six Core pages have no bar picture.
