findings.where: Header, every page
findings.what: The header reads 'Tropos', 'Lighting', 'Mantle', 'Contact': two product names and one kind of product. Nothing in it tells a new visitor that Tropos is a loudspeaker or Mantle a turntable.
findings.why_it_matters: A visitor who lands on an inner page reads the header first.
findings.fix: Kinds in the header ('Speakers', 'Turntable', 'Lighting'), or each name with its kind beside it.
findings.evidence: KEF's header reads 'Speakers, Subwoofers, Headphones, Accessories' (https://us.kef.com/); Linn's home tiles read 'Turntables, Network Music Players, Speakers' (https://www.linn.co.uk/us).
findings.verdict_evidence: Header links: 'Tropos' (/tropos), 'Lighting' (/lighting), 'Mantle' (/mantle), 'Contact'; behind 'Menu' on the phone. KEF's home page has 'Speakers', 'Subwoofers', 'Headphones', 'Accessories'; Linn's has 'Turntables', 'Network Music Players', 'Speakers'. Judgment: that a new visitor does not know the names.

findings.where: Whole site
findings.what: Between looking and writing a personal letter there is no smaller step: no way to be told when the first pair is built, no sheet to take away, no samples.
findings.why_it_matters: Most visitors to a product in development are not ready to ask for a quote today, and the site lets them leave without a trace.
findings.fix: One field at 'Write to us.': 'Tell me when the first pair is built.' A one-page sheet per product. Acrylic chips by mail are the owner's call.
findings.evidence: Tala 'NOTIFY ME WHEN AVAILABLE' (https://tala.co.uk/products/mantle-portable-lamp-in-claycourt-orange); OJAS 'Notify me when back in stock' (https://ojas.nyc/products/klipsch-x-ojas-ko-1); Roll & Hill 'ORDER SAMPLES' (https://www.rollandhill.com/products/cloud-pendant-14).
findings.verdict_evidence: The source has no form, no input other than the eight color radios, and none of 'notify', 'newsletter', 'subscribe', 'sample' or 'download'. Tala's page has 'Notify me when available' in its source and shows 'Out of stock'; OJAS has 'Notify me when back in stock'; Roll & Hill has 'ORDER SAMPLES'. Judgment: 'most visitors are not ready'.

findings.where: How pages and pictures are released
findings.what: The faults above are of three kinds a list catches: how many pictures each page has in each tint (Hemisphere: 9, 5, 4), how many grounds stand in one grid (three), and where each picture, marker and button leads (two bar pictures lead nowhere; one family tile of four leads to a list; the ask leads to another page). The pack's own index lists Hemisphere's nine pictures as 'every tint'.
findings.why_it_matters: The owner's sixth point: these should be caught before he sees them.
findings.fix: Three checks before anything goes live, run against the lists in this report: count each product's pictures in each tint against its set; put every grid's tiles side by side and compare the grounds; click every picture, marker and button on desktop and phone and write down where it lands.
findings.evidence: The scripts that did these three checks here: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/site-check/gallery.js; and homedom.js, clicks.js, ask.js, pagelinks.js in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/audit/work/merch/
findings.verdict_evidence: The facts hold: Hemisphere has 9, 5 and 4 pictures by tint; the family grid has three grounds; the two bar pictures on /lighting are not links; the Tropos family tile opens /tropos; the ask link opens /contact. INDEX.md lists Hemisphere's nine views under 'every tint'. The scripts it names exist. The three checks it proposes are judgment.

missed.where: Hemisphere product pages: HANGING row against the line under the name, the LIGHT row and the 'Over a table' caption
missed.what: HANGING says 'a 600 mm drop as standard, cut to length'. The line says 'Hung low over a table.', LIGHT gives 'about 340 lux on a table half a meter below' and the Ember caption says 'Half a meter over an oak table.' My arithmetic, not a measurement, on a ceiling and a table the page does not give: under a 2.44 m (8 ft) ceiling, over a 0.75 m table, half a meter over the table needs a drop of about 1.2 m; a 600 mm drop leaves the lamp about 1.1 m above the table, where the light on the table would be about a quarter of the figure given. The page does not say whether a longer cord is supplied or what 'cut to length' means.

plan.answer_for_owner:
Seven things, from 39 stores:

1. One ground for every product in a grid. Light, lamps off: Design Within Reach, Fritz Hansen, Louis Poulsen. Mid-tone, lamps lit: Santa & Cole, Gantri, Tala.
2. The product page opens on the product alone, then rooms: DWR, Knoll, Herman Miller, KEF. One set of rooms serves every color: DWR, Louis Poulsen, Muuto.
3. A lamp off and on from one camera: Louis Poulsen, &Tradition, Hem, Gantri.
4. A bright home, with furniture for size: a speaker pair around a console or fireplace (Klipsch, Avantgarde, KEF, U-Turn); a small lamp beside books (DWR, HAY, Carl Hansen).
5. Room pictures name their products by caption or corner button: HAY, &Tradition, Flos, DWR. None of the 35 home pages we studied has dots on its first picture; Vitra and KEF use them inside pages, at the object's edge.
6. Selling by inquiry: a starting price and the wait printed beside the ask: Apparatus, Lindsey Adelman, Allied Maker.
7. Sizes in inches, with a dimension drawing: Flos, Roll & Hill, Santa & Cole, OJAS.
sources: 1. Design Within Reach, ceiling lamps listing: https://www.dwr.com/lighting-ceiling?lang=en_US
2. Herman Miller, Eames Lounge Chair and Ottoman: https://store.hermanmiller.com/living-room-furniture-lounge-chairs-ottomans/eames-lounge-chair-and-ottoman/5667.html?lang=en_US
3. Louis Poulsen, Panthella Portable The Originals: https://www.louispoulsen.com/en-us/c/indoor-lighting/portable-lamps/panthella-portable-lamp-the-originals
5. Design Within Reach, home page: https://www.dwr.com/

owner_decisions.question: Which mailbox receives hello@earf.world?
owner_decisions.recommendation: Sign up for a mailbox or forwarder today and tell the site lane, which then adds the MX and SPF records and sends a test letter from outside.
owner_decisions.why: earf.world has no mail record (looked up at 10:44 UTC on 20 Nov). The address is the only way to buy, and every other fix to the ask leads to it. No test letter was sent, so that mail fails is read from DNS.

owner_decisions.question: Can a pair be ordered today, or not yet?
owner_decisions.recommendation: If you would quote someone who wrote today, say 'Not built yet. Write for a quote.' beside every ask and take 'not yet for sale' out of the link previews. If you would not, take 'Price on request', 'made to order' and 'we quote' off the pages and make the button 'Tell me when the first pair is built'. The pages already speak as if the first is true, so the first is the recommendation.
owner_decisions.why: The pages and their link previews say opposite things. OJAS takes orders on lots it has not built, puts 'Pre-Order' in the title and prints the plan beside the button.

owner_decisions.question: Which facts will you commit to beside the ask: a reply time, a starting price, the wait?
owner_decisions.recommendation: A reply time you will keep (Apparatus says two business days, Lindsey Adelman one). The state of the build in place of a wait until there is one. A starting price for the Tropos pair as soon as you have a number. Two lines on who answers and where the work is done.
owner_decisions.why: Apparatus, Lindsey Adelman and Allied Maker, who sell by inquiry, print a starting price and the wait beside the ask. The stores that print no price send the buyer to a dealer who quotes, and EARF has no dealer. With 'Price on request' alone a visitor cannot tell whether a pair costs five thousand dollars or fifty.

owner_decisions.question: One ground for every tile and first picture: the Tropos warm white with the lamps off, or a darker ground with the lamps lit?
owner_decisions.recommendation: The Tropos warm white, lamps off, the lit lamp as picture 2. Keep the dark ground for lit and detail pictures inside the lamp galleries.
owner_decisions.why: The Tropos has its eight on that ground, so this costs 24 renders (40 with the lit pairs); a darker ground means the Tropos set again too. Tinted acrylic shows its color by light passing through to a light ground; on the site's dark grounds the same tints go near-black. Lit lamps do not match the Tropos in tint, and you approved matching them when off (17 Nov). Design Within Reach, Fritz Hansen, Muuto, Hem and Louis Poulsen do it this way; Santa & Cole, Gantri and Tala use a mid-tone with lamps lit; Roll & Hill uses dark for every lamp. Bang & Olufsen keeps a deep color for detail pictures and never mixes it into a grid, which is the place for your deep grounds here.

owner_decisions.question: Keep the dots on the home page's first picture?
owner_decisions.recommendation: No. Put one line of names in the picture's bottom edge, each a link ('Tropos in Acid · Hemisphere in Ember · Core in Ember · Mantle in Ember'), and use dots with a small card on the room pictures inside the pages.
owner_decisions.why: None of the 35 stores the researchers opened marks its first picture. HAY, &Tradition and Flos name the products under the picture; Design Within Reach, Herman Miller, Knoll and Fritz Hansen use one corner button. Vitra and KEF use dots inside pages, at the object's edge, each opening a card. A line of names needs no placement for each crop and works the same on a phone.

owner_decisions.question: Which coined lines stay?
owner_decisions.recommendation: Keep 'A world of sound, in color.' Remove the eight mood lines under the color names ('The last light of the fire.' to 'Smoked glass, for after dark.') and keep the fact beside them ('Translucent red'). Remove the heading 'Each color is a place.' and let the eight pictures carry it. Shorten 'Eight colors, the full spectrum.' to 'Eight colors'.
owner_decisions.why: They are built like 'Drawn to be made.': a short coined sentence beside a picture or a fact that already says it. 'Bottle green. Keep out of reach.' sits over 'ACRYLIC Translucent bottle green'; 'Smoked glass' names the wrong material; Fog is clear and Smoke is gray, so the spectrum is not full. In the stores the line under a finish name is a material or price fact, or there is none. These lines are the brand's voice on color, so the call is yours.

standing_checklist: In every grid or row where two products stand side by side, do all the pictures share one ground, one light direction and one tile size?
With one tint chosen, do all four products read as that one color side by side?
Is every product whole and clear of the edges in its tile and its first picture at 1440, 1024 and 390 px wide, at rest and under the pointer?
Counted on the page itself and not from a list: does every tint of each product show the same views in the same order, and does the count match that product's written picture list?
Does every product page open on the product alone on the house ground, under a title that is the product's name, with one sentence that says what the product is?
Does every product have a picture in a home in light that lets the room be read, with something of known size in frame, and does each lamp have its off and on pair from one camera?
Clicked on a desktop and on a phone: does every picture, tile, marker and button open the product and the tint it shows?
Does every room picture name the products in it as links, and is every marker off the drivers, the lit shades, the record and other controls?
Is there no line beside a picture that says what the picture shows, and no new coined or mood line?

Does one visible button on every product page, on the first phone screen or fixed to its foot, open a letter that already names the product and the tint, and does a test letter from an outside account arrive?
Does every product and tint have an address that loads directly, without the opening animation, and previews with its own name and a picture of that product?
Do the page, the line beside the ask and the link preview say the same thing about whether it can be ordered, and does each picture's limit (render, 'Shown in Ember.') stand beside the picture?
Does a color click keep the view the visitor is on, and does one Back leave the product?
Are sizes and weights given in inches and pounds as well as metric, and do the figures agree with each other, with the labels inside the pictures and with the clear tint (Fog)?

Was each changed page set beside the same kind of page at two reference stores (for a lamp, Design Within Reach and Louis Poulsen; for the speaker, KEF and Klipsch), with each difference fixed or kept on purpose?
